Risk: No structured channel from solutions to delivery
Clarifying statement: If context gathered during the sale isn't handed over, delivery rebuilds it and discovery restarts from zero.
Client label: Context carries from sales into delivery

Risk: Solutions-stage risks/assumptions aren't captured in an inheritable form
Clarifying statement: Early risk signal surfaced pre-sale is lost at the handoff and must be rediscovered.

Risk: Commercial commitments aren't linked to their confidence basis
Clarifying statement: Delivery inherits scope/price promises the evidence doesn't yet support.

Risk: No defined engagement start (sale vs kickoff)
Clarifying statement: Evidence capture begins late, missing the richest early context.

Risk: Discovery produces narrative, not testable assumptions
Clarifying statement: Build begins on unvalidated ground; nothing can be checked.
Client label: Discovery produces testable assumptions, not just narrative

Risk: Highest-risk assumptions aren't identified first
Clarifying statement: Effort goes to low-risk areas while collapse risks stay untested.

Risk: No confidence gate defined for discovery→build
Clarifying statement: Work advances because time passed, not because uncertainty dropped.
Client label: A confidence gate governs discovery to build

Risk: Discovery scope is unbounded (tries to define the whole system)
Clarifying statement: Over-definition — the classic traditional-discovery failure.

Risk: Client expects 'discovery complete' as the deliverable
Clarifying statement: Tension with an evidence-gated exit the ADLC must reconcile.

Risk: Engineering isn't in discovery
Clarifying statement: Feasibility risk is deferred and surfaces late, in build.
Client label: Engineering validates feasibility from day one

Risk: Slices become features (many assumptions per test)
Clarifying statement: False confidence, slow learning; can't attribute the signal.

Risk: No reliability floor defined for agent-executed steps
Clarifying statement: Can't distinguish a real failure from an agent artifact.
Client label: Agent-produced work meets a defined reliability bar

Risk: No defined point where a human reviews agent output before it advances
Clarifying statement: Unvalidated agent work hardens into commitment.
Client label: Human review before agent work advances

Risk: Evidence/spike code gets hardened by default
Clarifying statement: Irreversible investment before confidence is earned.

Risk: No boundary between evidence-build and commitment-build
Clarifying statement: Engineers default to building; validation deprioritized.

Risk: Build assumes agent tooling/infra Sparq hasn't standardized
Clarifying statement: Build steps aren't reproducible across teams.

Risk: Prototype fidelity read as decision maturity
Clarifying statement: Polish implies commitment; exploration gets killed.

Risk: Signal isn't instrumented before a slice runs
Clarifying statement: Slices degrade into demos; confidence becomes subjective.
Client label: Findings are measured, not just demonstrated

Risk: No explicit decision at each gate (promote/iterate/pivot/stop)
Clarifying statement: Silent drift and implicit scaling.
Client label: Every gate ends in an explicit decision

Risk: Confidence updates aren't recorded
Clarifying statement: Cost model and scope rest on unstated assumptions.

Risk: Review cadence is calendar-driven, not evidence-triggered
Clarifying statement: Reviews fire when nothing changed, or miss when everything did.

Risk: No owner for gate discipline
Clarifying statement: Gates get skipped under delivery pressure.

Risk: 'Stop' isn't a socially permitted outcome
Clarifying statement: Failed hypotheses get quietly promoted instead of killed.

Risk: Evidence isn't captured in a durable substrate
Clarifying statement: Learning dies with the engagement; nothing compounds.
Client label: What we learn is captured and carried forward

Risk: Decisions captured without rationale
Clarifying statement: Future teams re-litigate — the reset tax.

Risk: No path to feed engagement learning back into the ADLC itself
Clarifying statement: The lifecycle doesn't improve; it only runs.

Risk: Handoff to delivery is static docs, not the evidence layer
Clarifying statement: Delivery can't see what's validated vs assumed.

Risk: No central engagement store (live state)
Clarifying statement: Evidence scattered across docs/Jira/Slack/code; traceability breaks.

Risk: Capture is manual only
Clarifying statement: Process too heavy to sustain; teams stop logging.

Risk: No retrieval surface
Clarifying statement: Captured evidence isn't usable at the moment of decision.

Risk: Artifact generation stays manual
Clarifying statement: Time freed by evidence-first work gets eaten by documentation.

Risk: Roles defined by artifact ownership, not evidence ownership
Clarifying statement: Evidence work falls to whoever holds the mental model — one person.

Risk: No role runs confidence/gate discipline
Clarifying statement: The governing mechanism has no owner.

Risk: Inter-function communication channels undefined
Clarifying statement: Coordination overhead replaces execution; PM becomes the single translator.

Risk: No shared vocabulary for confidence states
Clarifying statement: Teams mean different things by 'validated'; gates become arguments.

Risk: No stakeholder-facing progress surface for evidence work
Clarifying statement: Stakeholders demand the Gantt back; the model gets rejected.
Client label: Progress is visible without status theater

Risk: ADLC can't run inside fixed SOW/timeline (constrained mode)
Clarifying statement: A clean model that dies on contact with the contract.

Risk: Deliverables can't express confidence honestly
Clarifying statement: Forced definitive language = polished fiction, the failure the system exists to prevent.
Client label: Deliverables show what's proven vs. still uncertain

Risk: Client must adopt the methodology to benefit
Clarifying statement: Adoption friction kills it; value must land without client buy-in.

Risk: ADLC is a relabel of Evidence Work + SDLC
Clarifying statement: Swap/kill: remove the label — does anything change? If not, no new object.

Risk: 'Lifecycle' reintroduces phase/stage thinking
Clarifying statement: The frame fights the confidence-governed system it sits in.

Risk: Altitude undefined (Seam vs Fabric)
Clarifying statement: Audience, language, and artifacts fork unresolvably.

Risk: Running this pilot by hand won't surface tooling needs unless instrumented
Clarifying statement: Pilot yields the ADLC but not the tooling map.
